column5: Carpet underlay made from reclaimed urethane foam pieces. Source metadata describes 9 mm roll stock; this nominal stock thickness is identity metadata, not the instrument-measured sample thickness or a universal product specification. Exact scrap composition, binder, foam density distribution, blowing agent and manufacturer grade are unknown. No moisture, contact pressure, isotropy, compression-response, aging, strength, expansion, fire/degradation or service-temperature law is inferred from these thermal experiments.

The Wet label in raw filenames denotes unconditioned samples kept indoors at 22 +/- 3 degC and relative humidity 40 +/- 20 percent. It does not mean water-saturated, nor does it supply exact sample moisture or zero moisture. These specimens are not assigned the source's separate oven-dried condition. The general conductivity method is ASTM C518 with through-thickness upward heat flow; the general capacity method is ASTM C1784-20 with equal-temperature plate steps. Applied contact pressure, calibrated instrument uncertainty, specimen-axis mapping and cross-property covariance are not provided. Conductivity and capacity are distinct runs; joint thermal use is conditional on treating the selected product/conditioning population as representative, not proof of identical coupons or independent measurements.

column5: The 3 complete native volume-capacity results are averaged at each source temperature. Temperatures round to 0.1 degC as in the primary reduction, giving 10,20,30,40 degC; conversion to kelvin adds exactly 273.15. Across-specimen sample SD is sqrt(sum((C_i-mean_C)^2)/(3-1)); it is retained as a discrete statistic, not a confidence interval or instrument uncertainty. Extra computed digits are arithmetic, not extra measurement resolution. Linear interpolation of mean C(T) and the published Cp(T) is an authored local approximation to finite-step estimates; interpolation error is unquantified and extrapolation is disallowed.

Rebond_Foam_Carpet_Pad_Density_Wet_R1.csv, Rebond_Foam_Carpet_Pad_Density_Wet_R2.csv and Rebond_Foam_Carpet_Pad_Density_Wet_R3.csv report densities 84,84,89 kg/m3. Corresponding masses are 34.4,34,21.5 g and volumes are 412,406.5,240.1 cm3. The primary reduction averages the reported rounded density column to 85.66666666666667 kg/m3; recomputing mass divided by volume would change that normalization. Density measurement temperature is not stated. This scalar is a reference normalization input without a temperature validity domain, not a measured density(T) curve or a constant density law.

The mean native volume-capacity values divided by mean reported density are rounded to whole J/(kg K): 1722,1759,1758,1820 at 10,20,30,40 degC. Published SD 110,141,103,147 J/(kg K) is native capacity sample SD divided by the same mean density and rounded to whole units. This does not propagate density scatter, covariance or calibration uncertainty. Cp, native C and normalization density are algebraically related, not independent measurements; the rounded published Cp values remain distinct from unrounded native C.

column5: 3 specimens each provide three repeated cycles at each mean temperature: 9 readings per temperature, not 9 independent specimens. Raw measured mean temperatures round to 15,65 degC. The primary script pools the readings, rounds means and sample SD to 0.001 W/(m K), and publishes means 0.037,0.044 with SD 0.001,0.001. A printed SD of 0.000 is rounding, not zero uncertainty. Linear interpolation between mean-temperature groups is an authored approximation with unquantified error. Only actual groups are retained; blank cells from aligned condition tables do not create measurements.

The thermal-conductivity curve requires mean-test-temperature-as-local-model=1. It explicitly substitutes the finite-gradient apparent HFM conductivity for a local scalar through-thickness coefficient at the same numerical temperature. This is an authored engineering approximation, not deconvolution of the 20 K plate difference, a point measurement or proof of isotropy. The apparent-thermal-conductivity curve retains its native test-mean-temperature axis.
